| | The Trump administration and DOGE's next target: veterans. Trump and Elon Musk plan to cut over 80,000 workers from the Department of Veteran Affairs in the coming weeks. This will take a sledgehammer to the basic care and services our veterans rely on in their daily lives. The VA provides veterans with everything from rehabilitation for injuries sustained in combat, to health care, to mental health services, and so much more. It's a lifeline for those who have bravely put their lives on the line to defend our country and our freedoms. It's just the latest example of how the Trump-Musk administration is doing everything in its power to make our country less safe. Throwing the basic care and rights of veterans into the garbage can is a surefire way to make our families and our communities less safe. Elon Musk and his DOGE cronies have even fired **thousands** of veterans across government departments. And what did the White House Counsel have to say about people who bravely served their country being fired without notice? **She questioned whether they were even fit to be employed in the first place.** **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/103692559/532932866/-2044921950?refcode=2025-03-11-veterans&recurring=0&amount=5&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=31c2a0e3-d4fe-ef11-90cd-0022482a9fb7&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMWMyYTBlMy1kNGZlLWVmMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=WMcj68U62SbuYYFA_F8y4cBL3vpbtXvUvORzLjTgTF4=)****I'll tell you who's not fit to have a job in this government:****_anyone who treats veterans like pawns in a political game._** Service members made the ultimate sacrifice to keep us safe, and Donald Trump and Republicans are thanking them by ripping away their health care and safety net. We owe those who have taken up the uniform so much more. I'll do everything I can to fight Trump's planned cuts to the VA, and I'll work to ensure that the stories of veterans wrongly fired by Trump and Musk are known. name: Kimberly Bretches
subject: Life behind bars could be his “reward.”
body:
| | | The same city that gave Chance this award is trying to put him in prison for life for doing his job.
---
| |
---
Dear Peter, That's me and my husband, Officer Chance Bretches in the picture I've sent you...
---
[](http://links.standingstrongamerica.com/u/click?_t=29c3b6e742c849fabbcc130432510e66&_m=1fe96b5934504129b289d44c706ce62a&_e=CHdpiFJsYoWTuQoLTI9dq05LCWocN76v5w2maaF63KYoolSHasczzdPAgfYuePJnmpFkUbQmJ-ztRqi-87IPf8k0L0jLfQCZgZMA6VWSN67aSrzlkLETX0EpYzJK3rLQG2nC1JxdnnfS9LyZybVg_vbBSz-YWBL3C0z7iy_eccPxIyQKH1sxGj8jb6G9rF9yhciaCWSmxbybr6AVEdjRMIuhMBIAA36cqkKkRcR6L38IOAQ6NTpdNH89RK2-L1g2DkeB6vdMU-CAnrWlPW13Ds4CUyxwwZ2gOQ-qwPQXEeFSRF53ZfDCd3DRU27mut_QHCshc5gqXc1DsfRtVZJiUxZdw_LqLl-QD3GIVUh71X0KXTjp22lMBkXHfgrZNrfW)
---
...a picture we took on the day Chance received the Lifesaving Medal With Valor for rescuing a driver from a crashed car that had caught on fire. This photo used to be one of my favorites. Now looking at it makes me cry. Because in July, the same city that gave Chance this award... ...will try to lock him up for life for doing his job. I should explain. For nearly 13 years, Chance has been a decorated police officer with the Austin, Texas Police Department. But in May of 2020, our lives were turned upside down. You probably remember what it was like in our country after George Floyd. Violent, fiery anti-police protests were sweeping through cities. Every step of the way, they were cheered on by radical politicians, Soros-funded prosecutors, and the Mainstream Media who lied to us and said, with a straight face, that these riots were "mostly peaceful." It was especially bad here in Austin, Texas. For three nights in a row, angry, anti-cop mobs rampaged through downtown, smashing windows, burning police cars, and looting stores. The crowd attacked officers like my husband who were trying to keep the peace, pelting them with rocks, bricks, and even lit fireworks. On the third night, things got even worse. Protestors shut down interstate, and a crazed mob surrounded Police Headquarters. Chance and his fellow officers knew that if they didn't restore order quickly, the headquarters, and maybe even the entire city, might burn to the ground. Following their training, they fired non-lethal weapons – the same "beanbag guns" that police have used for years to break up riots – to stop the violence before it got out of hand. The mob slunk off. And my husband made it home safe and sound. What I didn’t know then was that this nightmare wasn't over for us. Far from it. Unknown to Chance and the other officers on duty that night, an anti-police protestor was hit by one of my husband's non-lethal rounds. They claimed they were injured and lost part of their finger. And for that... ...the county prosecutor charged my husband with "aggravated assault by a public servant" -- a charge punishable by life in prison. This is the upside-down world we live in now. A world where lawless thugs who fling rocks at police and try to burn our city to the ground get off scot-free... ...while law-abiding officers get criminal charges and face life in prison for following their training and breaking up a mob of rioters. What are cops like my husband supposed to do when faced with this kind of out-of-control violence?! When Chance told me about the charges, my emotions went from disbelief to anger to despair...and back again. But it all started to make sense when we learned that the prosecutor in this case owes his election to a wad of campaign cash from none other than radical Leftist billionaire George Soros. That was when I realized that the anti-cop crowd is trying to get revenge on my husband. They don't care if my husband is innocent. They'll do everything in their power to make cops pay. It makes me wonder why anyone would ever sign up to join law enforcement these days. But nearly 13 years ago, my husband did. And he did it because helping innocent people is in his blood. His brother is a firefighter. His dad is a 34-year police veteran. My husband is a youth leader at our church and plays guitar in the worship band. He's served on mission trips -- planting churches, planning vacation Bible schools, and sharing the Gospel. And he's done his job as a police officer with honor and dignity, without a single mark against his record. Chance put his life on the line to protect our city from a violent, unhinged mob... ...and life behind bars and could be his "reward." Even if my husband's good name is cleared there is no way we could hope to pay the mountain of legal bills. Thankfully, by God's grace, there is one group who has stepped up to help us -- the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF). If you've ever heard of LELDF, you know that their record has made them a policemen's best friend. Jason Johnson and the LELDF board organize and fund the successful legal defense of good cops wrongly charged for crimes -- like my husband. LELDF hires the best attorneys and secures expert witnesses who will testify to the truth -- without being influenced by political paybacks. And now they've agreed to help Chance. My friend, you've read my letter this far so I'm going to ask as boldly as I can: Will you help Chance, too? _**[Would you help by sending a one-time gift to LELDF so this amazing group can defend my husband and the other good police officers who have wrongly accused?](http://links.standingstrongamerica.com/u/click?_t=29c3b6e742c849fabbcc130432510e66&_m=1fe96b5934504129b289d44c706ce62a&_e=CHdpiFJsYoWTuQoLTI9dq05LCWocN76v5w2maaF63KYoolSHasczzdPAgfYuePJnmpFkUbQmJ-ztRqi-87IPf8k0L0jLfQCZgZMA6VWSN67aSrzlkLETX0EpYzJK3rLQG2nC1JxdnnfS9LyZybVg_vbBSz-YWBL3C0z7iy_eccPxIyQKH1sxGj8jb6G9rF9yhciaCWSmxbybr6AVEdjRMIuhMBIAA36cqkKkRcR6L38bRUARmtUmeFW5CvbKTvKb9_hhRUOmfuf9bpqgk_5OC6SVCw0kCHKNHvN8yPFGxOb9ig658fLpRiboL-3j4y0HXZKuMYDwaqwgqDvvAj5TYp76TxCoWC_2hZwOTNBT4ZhCWMuGhtT3Y4IvsFFEKJTd)**_** ** You see, LELDF is a non-profit organization. This photo used to be one of my favorites. Now looking at it makes me cry. Because in July, the same city that gave Chance this award... ...will try to lock him up for life for doing his job. I should explain. For nearly 13 years, Chance has been a decorated police officer with the Austin, Texas Police Department. But in May of 2020, our lives were turned upside down. You probably remember what it was like in our country after George Floyd. Violent, fiery anti-police protests were sweeping through cities. Every step of the way, they were cheered on by radical politicians, Soros-funded prosecutors, and the Mainstream Media who lied to us and said, with a straight face, that these riots were "mostly peaceful." It was especially bad here in Austin, Texas. For three nights in a row, angry, anti-cop mobs rampaged through downtown, smashing windows, burning police cars, and looting stores. The crowd attacked officers like my husband who were trying to keep the peace, pelting them with rocks, bricks, and even lit fireworks. On the third night, things got even worse. Protestors shut down interstate, and a crazed mob surrounded Police Headquarters. Chance and his fellow officers knew that if they didn't restore order quickly, the headquarters, and maybe even the entire city, might burn to the ground. Following their training, they fired non-lethal weapons – the same "beanbag guns" that police have used for years to break up riots – to stop the violence before it got out of hand. In Minnesota, we proudly identify as members of the Democratic-Farmer-Labor (DFL) Party, a unique identity from a rich history. The DFL was established in 1944 through the merger of the Minnesota Democratic Party and the Farmer-Labor Party, a progressive movement that championed the rights of farmers and laborers in the early 20th century. This merger created a party deeply rooted in advocating for working families and progressive values, a legacy that continues to influence Minnesota's political landscape today.

During the last legislative session, Minnesota's DFL-led trifecta demonstrated the profound impact of unified leadership. We enacted historic protections for reproductive rights, expanded voting access, strengthened labor protections, advanced climate initiatives, and invested significantly in working families. However, while the nation trended right, we held our ground in Minnesota--but the Minnesota House ended up in a tie, underscoring the critical need to protect our progress and continue building on our achievements.

Throughout the weekend, attendees will engage with campaign strategists, elected officials, and grassroots organizers to explore what it takes to build enduring. As we look ahead to 2026 and beyond, this meeting serves as a call to action for Young Democrats to apply some of the lessons learned in Minnesota nationwide. The journey to power extends beyond winning elections--it's about building a lasting movement. Join us in **Minneapolis from May****9-1****1** as we chart the future of Democratic leadership, grassroots organizing, and the pursuit of progress. We look forward to seeing you in the Twin Cities! subject: They Gutted Public Education. Now We Must Fight Back!

body:
They actually did it. They gutted the Department of Education,

| | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/43357e0170ee/they-gutted-public-education-now-we-must-fight-back?e=606d7e9aa2)
---
| | | | |
---
[](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=7d16127739&e=606d7e9aa2)
|

**Friend,**
They actually did it. They **gutted** the Department of **Education** , slashed **thousands of jobs** , and turned their backs on the very system that built this country and gave millions of Americans, including me, the chance at a **better life.**
Let me be clear: This isn’t about cutting bureaucracy. This is an **attack** on working families, on our teachers, and on **every child in Southside Virginia** and across the commonwealth who depends on public education to build a better future.
I was raised in a small town where the **coal mines were calling my name** from the county over. Without strong public schools, I might have had no other option. But because public education gave me the foundation to go to college, become a doctor, and serve my community, I was able to build **a different future**. That’s what they’re trying to take away from the next generation.
This is not about efficiency, it’s about making sure only the wealthy get a quality education while the rest of us are left behind.
With these devastating cuts, here’s what happens next:
* Schools in rural communities like ours will suffer the most.
* Special education and vocational training programs will be gutted.
* Teachers will be paid even less while expected to do even more.
* Federal protections for students will vanish overnight.

I refuse to accept this.
**Public education made me who I am,** and I won’t stand by while they dismantle it. That’s why I’m running for the House of Delegates; to fight back and protect our schools, our students, and our future.
But I can’t do it alone. If you believe in **strong public school** s, in giving every child a **fair shot** , and in protecting the future of Southside Virginia, then I need your help.
**Will you donate today to help us take this fight to Richmond? Every dollar counts.**
---
| [DONATE](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=d7db61d2a4&e=606d7e9aa2)
---
| We still have a chance to stop them, but only if all **work together for what’s right**. Thank you for standing with me.
Sincerely,
**Dr. Gary Miller**
Democratic CandidateHouse of Delegates, District 49

subject: I’m running for governor and I want to explain why

body:
President Trump, his allies, and Republicans across the country will all be watching to see the strength of our movement.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=39524%2E3422442%2E4mzP6W)
I just announced that I’m running to be California’s next governor! Here are 3 quick things you should know about who I am and why I’m running:
1. One of my top priorities will be **standing up to Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans.** When Trump threatens Californians—whether it’s by withholding disaster aid or attacking our LGBTQ+ community—I’ll always stand up to his bullying and fight back.

2. Our state faces real challenges. From housing and health care costs that are out of control, to a rapidly changing climate—we need new ideas and leaders with the backbone to fight for what’s right.

3. I held the first Trump Administration accountable in Congress and got real results **(sometimes with my whiteboard, sometimes without!)**. My questioning of Trump officials secured free COVID testing for every American in the earliest days of the pandemic, and I’m proud to have passed into law bills that hold Big Oil and Big Pharma accountable for ripping off taxpayers.

I didn’t make the decision to run lightly, but Trump is too serious of a threat to be ignored. President Trump, his allies, and Republicans across the country will all be watching to see the strength of our movement. **[That’s why we set a $500,000 goal and why I’m asking if you can chip in.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20250311_5_ak?refcode=em20250311-39524&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39524_3422442_4mzP6W&akid=39524%2E3422442%2E4mzP6W)**

I’d be so grateful to earn your support. With so much at stake, it’s going to take every single one of us.
Katie Porter

Katie is running to be California’s next governor because California and our country need a leader who will stand up to Trump to lower costs, protect our rights, and combat climate change. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4g-em-footer?refcode=em20250311-39524&amounts=&t=3&refcode2=39524_3422442_4mzP6W&akid=39524%2E3422442%2E4mzP6W)**

They think you and I will be so relieved to see the border secure again and criminal illegal aliens deported, that you and I will be oblivious to this threat lying dormant under our very eyes.No way.My name is Rebecca Weber. It’s us against the swamp, Peter. We need your support.

| | | Hey Peter,

This is Troy Downing from Montana. My story is one of service, sacrifice, and a commitment to the American Dream.

In the ’90s, I built a successful tech company that merged with Yahoo!. But when America was attacked on September 11th, I gave it all up to serve my country in the U.S. Air Force.

For eight years, I flew combat search and rescue missions, risking my life to save wounded soldiers on the battlefield. When I returned to Montana, I knew I wasn't done fighting for America. That's why I ran for Congress—**to take on the tough battles and stand up for the American Dream that our President and his allies are fighting to restore.**

As a new member of the House, I'm proud to be a voice for conservatives who are tired of the radical Left's attempts to undermine our nation's foundations. I've faced down terrorists and hostile fire, so I'm not intimidated by the Swamp in Washington or the liberal elites who want to silence us.

But I know that this fight is far from over. The Democrats will stop at nothing to obstruct President Trump's agenda and push their radical policies, and it's going to take patriots like you and me to hold the line. I'm counting on your support to keep fighting to achieve our vision for a stronger, safer America.

## Southwest Kills Free Checked Bags
Southwest Airlines unveiled sweeping changes Tuesday, [scrapping its iconic “two bags fly free”](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx00LFutDAQBOCnMZ2Rdw34rnDxN3T3tymRbZZjE4NP2DmLt49In3ZG-jSaj8f0cBx5f_53G9mypAkV9lJpCTjNjuM5dc1sFyIk3ZAF04ExnTZDs1o9aN2ru_He684pAg_odSA0vYKe7g3bS1MaEBSo_tbeQC3ODWYIAKYPXnSKZi7paD8T72WlJZ7pTUcb0tZEu5byykL_EzgKHGutbdh9uEqB40ULHJUWOAIIHHP6LmulXKTjI_JOWXr3lAtRliVJ7zIHSSHtaTtlXV250q891XYtW2wOO78qx8h5MKJTz81x_N1R_vrlbfEnAAD__3v_Y9M) policy and introducing baggage fees for most passengers starting May 28. The airline is also launching a no-frills basic economy fare that prohibits free flight changes, ending another customer-friendly practice that sets Southwest apart from competitors. The shift was driven by a push by activist hedge fund Elliott Investment Management to boost revenue. It earned praise from at least one competitor: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby called it "[the slaying of the sacred cow.](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx00LGO6yAQheGnwR3RMGBwCorbuMttt7SwPbZnRSACkshvv8r22386R_q_btMtcOS0_w938m3LEwL2ErRUOK2B4zmZbvUbEZLuyCtnlHNGO9sdHnsLYQFLcz8PVzCgr9oOCma9mavuVcf-swZaoQIF_XAZFGwhWGcXpVy_zMIArdxyuXxnTu2gLZ75ReWy5HsX_dHaowr9T-AocGwHPT6q7s_zAwSOid5V4Fjzsx1vqk0GLpETVTmHXW5EVXJan7WVUxYKS-OcBI5d8evjzTFytU4Y2O-B4-9n-6vBy-NPAAAA__-yfF73)" Travelers buying anything but the top-tier Business Select fare will pay to check bags—likely around $35 each, matching competitors. All tickets still include a free carry-on.

name: Josh W.
subject: I’m the teacher who’ll bring GOP to its knees in 2025
body:
| | | | | | [](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wr5gm-vke2y5-kyd76rh3/)
---
# **I’m the teacher who’ll bring GOP to its knees in 2025**
---
| [](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wr5gm-vke2y6-kyd76rh4/)
---
| | | | friend, If you and I haven't met yet, my name is **Josh Weil**. I'm a single father, Democrat, and public school teacher running in the Special Election for Florida's 6th Congressional District -**_the bellwether first election of 2025._** As we begin to hit our stride after a whirlwind first few weeks of this campaign, I haven’t yet had the chance to sit down and write out the story of who I am & why I’m running so let me tell you about why you should put your belief into this scrappy campaign that _stands to topple the GOPs razor thin 1-vote majority._ My career has been **_defined_** by work with at-risk or post risk populations in public schools. I worked for three years in juvenile detention under the FL Department of Juvenile Justice, then for two years at University Behavioral Center, a residential mental health hospital for teens. In these programs, kids were typically _5 years behind grade level_ and the programs were _extremely_ underfunded and under-resourced. As a result I had to wear a bunch of different hats - teacher, therapist, parent, and more. **It’s a helluva a job (literally),** and it’s not for everybody, but I am proud to have made a tangible impact with these students and this experience was _foundational_ in making me the teacher that I am today. I now work in Florida’s Osceola County public schools where I am on the leadership team of Kissimmee Middle School - a title one school (schools which have a high population of low income families and in turn receive lots of extra supplemental funding, all students receive supplemental funding). On the leadership team of Kissimmee: I’m an instructional coach for teachers, the Dean of Students where I handle behavior issues with students and families, and the MTSS coordinator - a role required under education law where I monitor/track student data across the school and then coordinate interventions and individualized education plans (IEPs) for students who are underperforming. In my first year where I oversaw Math, scores went down in every category at my school **_except_ math** which went up one point. In my 2nd year, I oversaw all of STEM where we made major gains in both categories and became the __**_highest gaining_** __ **_school_** __ in the whole county/district for that category. I have devoted my life’s work to **solving challenges that seem insurmountable to most** , to uplifting students and classrooms that society and our GOP state legislature have written off. So when I read that a special election would be held in my community for a vacant House seat following a Trump cabinet appointment, I saw an opportunity to tackle a challenge that I am uniquely qualified to take on and conquer. Before our launch, we were warned by Doubting Thomases that the Democratic base was burnt out, defeated, and apathetic in the aftermath of Kamala Harris’s defeat. We were told that we would be hard pressed to find people who would donate and or volunteer on this race. _They told us to give up._ My belief then and ever more so now is that when the chips are down and we’re backed into a corner is when we fight the hardest—and**now I am vindicated _every day_ as Democrats from across the US pour in to _fight with us_**. [**_Together we can rob the GOP of their 1-vote majority and restore hope to a movement reeling from our 2024 defeat - can you make a donation today to help us rapidly scale this campaign in time for our April 1st election?_**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wr5gm-vke2y7-kyd76rh5/)
---
| [Chip in $10](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wr5gm-vke2y8-kyd76rh6/)
---
| [$26 for 2026](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wr5gm-vke2y9-kyd76rh7/)
---
| [Chip in $100](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wr5gm-vke2ya-kyd76rh7/)
---
| [RUSH $250](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wr5gm-vke2yb-kyd76rh8/)
---
Thank you for being a part of this movement to stop Project 2025 and send a teacher—not a book banner—to Congress. This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, and we _cannot_ afford to miss it.
---
|
---
Yours in the fight, Josh Weil Democrat for Florida’s 6th

### **I applied for a film grant from Vimeo, Red, and Nikon**
---
**Funding Proposal for Vimeo Short Film Grant | Presented by Nikon | RED****The funds awarded by the Vimeo Short Film Grant would be essential in elevating** _**Frozen Odds: The Game of Alaska's Election**_**to a professional standard that captures the complexity and emotional depth of Alaska's 2022 election. While I have invested in key equipment such as the RED Scarlet-W, RED Komodo 6K, and high-quality audio gear, additional resources are crucial to enhance production value and effectively convey the film's message.****Grant funds would be allocated as follows:**
1. **Travel & Location Shoots: Capturing Alaska’s vast and remote landscapes is critical to visually telling this story. Funds would support travel to key locations such as Anchorage, Fairbanks, and smaller rural communities where the impact of the election was deeply felt.**
2. **Cinematography & Visual Effects: To illustrate complex voting mechanics like Ranked Choice Voting, funds would enable the creation of clear, animated visual explanations that simplify the process for viewers. This is vital for ensuring the film is accessible to all audiences.**
3. **Post-Production & Editing: Funds will allow me to secure a professional colorist and sound designer to refine the final product, ensuring consistency in visual tone and immersive audio quality.**
4. **Interviews & Expert Commentary: The grant will support travel and technical costs for conducting interviews with election officials, political experts, and grassroots campaigners whose insights are crucial to telling this story.**

**With this support, I can create a powerful, visually striking documentary that reveals the challenges of Alaska’s 2022 election and explores what this experience means for democracy across America.**
---
#### **Frozen Odds -**
**Spending the money I did on this camera setup was to capture Alaska politics like never before.****Alaska — vast, untamed, and unpredictable. Beneath its snow-covered peaks and icy rivers lies a political battlefield unlike any other. This is the story they didn’t want you to know.****Powerful names — Lisa Murkowski, Hansjörg Wyss, Arabella Advisors, and George Soros — echo through the corridors of influence, shaping the future of the Last Frontier. From the manipulation of Ranked Choice Voting to the backdoor funding of initiatives like the Minimum Wage Increase, Alaska has become a testing ground — a proving ground — for tactics designed to tilt democracy itself.****Groups like Salmon State, Outdoor Alliance, and the Alaska Venture Fund, Alaskans For Better Elections, No on 2, etc. have operated quietly, weaving a web of influence across the state's political landscape. What seemed like grassroots efforts were anything but — and the connections go far deeper than anyone imagined.****This isn't just about Alaska. It’s a warning to the rest of America.****Help bring this story to life, flying experts to Alaska, traveling the state for interviews. We have already raised 30% what we expected for the entire film to cost.****A huge Thank You,****Phil Izon**

#### **ANNOUNCEMENT : RC Maxwell Joins Frozen Odds as Featured Expert**
**We’re excited to announce that RC Maxwell, a fearless journalist and advocate against Ranked Choice Voting (RCV), will be featured in Frozen Odds, a groundbreaking documentary on Alaska’s citizen-led fight to repeal RCV.****RC Maxwell has an incredible story to tell. Years ago, he exposed Sen. Lisa Murkowski’s ties to RCV, helping reveal the system’s deeper implications. His investigative work with Project Veritas, with James O’Keefe, played a key role in spreading awareness about the dangers of RCV. He has since continued his work with at Newsmax, even interviewing me last year as we battled RCV in Alaska.****Personally, RC Maxwell was pivotal in my journey to challenge RCV. His early reporting helped shape my understanding of the issue, ultimately leading me to write the repeal and lead the grassroots movement against RCV in Alaska. Over the years, I’ve had the privilege of meeting him at CPAC and in Arizona, where I was educating others on the dangers of RCV.****We are honored to have RC Maxwell join us in filming Frozen Odds this summer. His firsthand experience and relentless commitment to election integrity will bring critical insights to this documentary.****Stay tuned—Frozen Odds is coming soon to uncover the truth behind Alaska’s fight for fair elections!**
---
#### **ANNOUNCEMENT: Captain Seth Keshel and Dr. Chris Mattmann Join Frozen Odds Movie as Featured Experts**
**We’re honored to announce that Seth Keshel, MBA, will be featured in Frozen Odds, the powerful documentary on Alaska’s citizen-led fight against Ranked Choice Voting (RCV).****Seth Keshel is a former Army Captain of Military Intelligence and Afghanistan veteran. His analytical method of election forecasting and analytics is known worldwide, and he has been commended by President Donald J. Trump for his work in the field. He most recently made headlines by correctly forecasting a 312-226 Trump victory in the Electoral College, with accurate picks in all 56 races for electoral votes.****Captain Keshel proposes 10 Points to True Election Integrity and has identified Ranked Choice Voting as one of the eight cardinal sins of election administration. He toured Alaska in the spring of 2022 while fighting the information battle associated with promoting election integrity.****In Frozen Odds, Captain Keshel will bring his expert analysis and firsthand experience to expose the flaws of RCV and its impact on election integrity.****Dr. Chris Mattmann Joins Frozen Odds as Featured Expert****We’re thrilled to announce that Dr. Chris Mattmann, a leading AI and data expert, will be featured in Frozen Odds, a powerful documentary on Alaska’s citizen-led fight against Ranked Choice Voting (RCV).****Dr. Mattmann’s career is nothing short of extraordinary. He is the Chief Data and AI Officer at UCLA, former Chief Technology and Innovation Officer at NASA JPL, and President of Mattmann.ai. An accomplished author and industry leader, he has played key roles in advancing AI, big data, and technology across multiple fields.****With firsthand experience in RCV from his time at the Apache Software Foundation, Dr. Mattmann will break down its flaws in Frozen Odds, sharing his expert insights and concerns based on real-world applications.****Stay tuned—Frozen Odds is coming soon to reveal the truth behind Alaska’s fight for fair elections.**

**Starting a film project for Amazon Prime, YouTube, etc. – Frozen Odds How do you take on $15 million with nothing but determination, grassroots organizing, and a clipboard? Frozen Odds is a gripping documentary that uncovers the raw power of citizen-led initiatives in Alaska. Following the journey of a small but determined movement, this film reveals how everyday people—outspent 100 to 1 by out-of-state interests—rallied together to challenge the system. Led by an Alaskans for Alaskans who helped write the law and push it to the ballot, this battle wasn’t just about policy—it was about democracy in its purest form. With 400+ volunteers braving the cold, gathering 42,000 signatures when only 26,000 were needed, they proved that people—not money—should shape the laws that govern them. Through intimate interviews, on-the-ground footage, and stunning Alaskan landscapes, Frozen Odds captures the high-stakes struggle against political elites (aka Lisa Murkowski and George Soros, etc.) and the enduring spirit of grassroots activism. Though the campaign fell just 700 votes short out of 320,000, it laid the groundwork for a new wave of initiatives—this time, with three fresh petitions ready to take the fight forward. In a world where billionaires and lobbyists try to control the political process, Frozen Odds asks a bold question: What happens when ordinary citizens refuse to back down?**

## Killeen Student Fatally Stabbed
A 14-year-old girl, [identified by relatives as Serenity Baker](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00LGOrCAUxvGnwQ4DRxmuBcVt6GbbLc1BDkoGZSLMOL79xu23_ie_fPm-7-MdY4rb_IUrmfoJeQQBiouOSxg9xnSOfeONE36QDRmpe6m17kA1i4GBqAc14U0NwuubApKafAgCxeQ1NNFcmOgkSKE0dK2Cf476oINzA2FA1gvysea9rQtV-mAJ6cxv2tspr00yS63Pwrr_DCwDexxH-zjq54oM7GUzsKJjYKVkYOccXptfiReq_PXkAdeYTl5opy3Wkzt80M7nuCcesGK6WkXnyPNHTIlo47F4XqYl58TANrvxzyOmFMtNs17MK8b0u6z-edXbwE8AAAD__yupbKs), was fatally stabbed by another student at Roy J. Smith Middle School in Killeen on Monday. Baker reportedly [got into a dispute](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLGO5CAQRL8GZ1jQ2IsdEFxCtpdeaDVDM4PEmBX0rsd_f_Lkm1Qlpaqn-ve5fWIueb__xSc5fqW6gYJZKiM1bBFzObdpiC6ouOqBnLaTttYamIeHo4RmpbQoCDiroG1IZr7d1hiWAFPCIburTBkNWs0WzDjDEmhKNoWwEiYUk6KYubaRH8T0wp7KWX-ojbf6HIp7MH91Yf4I8AL8cRzjd0euEc8rIMB3ru0U4Hc6-mXIue4C_LUrwCsjwGt9ySRPwiZrifKeW5EJGUs5ZWcMgaLs_B1pZ4mtUWeK8o0jwC8AH0qvVikrwA_Nxa8jl5L7hxWTuj8xlzct_3rfj4P_AQAA__8cjHFc) with a classmate, another 14-year-old girl, prior to the stabbing. She was pronounced dead at a local hospital, and the unnamed suspect was taken into custody by campus police. Following the incident, the school went into lockdown, and students were transported to a nearby church to be picked up. Classes at the school were [canceled until March 24](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLGO8yAQhJ8Gd1iwYBMXFH9Dl7-90lrMOkYhJjJcHL_9ySmuu2aa-TQzmq_reMWY4nr7jw-y9T3nEQR0XCguYQwY0zHqJlgvwiAbstJoaYxR0DWLlTjpXvYDdgOpi5gx6EkO3dx70JMC00R7hgklQYrOgGo7uHjSs5m9HwhnZFpQiDVvbV2o0hvLnI78oq2d8qNJdqn1WZj6x8AxcPu-t_eC9TQZuJX2wsClPGFi4M4qBk4oBk7KUzQ_CDeeU-ClfgdaKy8VvafA7zElChwrL9OSc-L-4LjmutD2y34YWvkzpzgRL3gwcM1mw3OPKcXSG6bF7YExfdbWP-97WfgJAAD__yiScnI), after the district’s spring break. Other Killeen ISD schools remain open. The school board [held an emergency meeting](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00DFv5CAQBeBfg7tZwQDLbkFxjbtce-VqgGGNAiayuXX870-Jrk396T3pvT9vjzcqtazP39TYj8_cHyjRgtSg8JGo1PNhpuSDTHc1sVfOKOecRjstXpsb2xCRJSprJbmrye6WKAbJLiJPxX-VSa1QSetQXyzeApvscgh3pkzCSE5l9O0yFh78SXuuZ3_xdom9TdUvY3zsQv8SOAucj-O4vEdex-uLBc60jRIrC5xXPnaBc-yt_V3LOAXO76VW5hXKnmCPS-8VQqctATfenrzGExrzKOsTGm1xAaUgMaV6wj4ohG8oKVX-Hxc4WykBrzGjQg0m3ywYd70DRUPATmGke1BWx2nz6eMotZb96oSRz0alfm8aP5788vgvAAD__wzjfzo) yesterday morning to hear from the community and provide an update on security measures currently in effect. "_Our hearts are heavy as we navigate this difficult time together_ ," said Killeen ISD Superintendent Dr. Jo Ann Fey.
## Bags Don't Fly Free Anymore
Dallas-based Southwest Airlines announced Tuesday it would [charge customers to check their bags](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00LFu8yAUBeCnwRsWXOAnGRj-xVu6drQu5hKjYhMZGpK3r9y96znSp6PzeZtvmHLa7x-4kWuvWGYQYLhQXMIcMOX3rIfgvAhXOZCTVktrrQIzrE5gDNbSRQok1Fc0QpkLLkFFbYzxakjuxISSIIWxoEYDF0862uj9lTAi04JCauUY20qNXlhjfpcnHeNStiG7tbVHZeo_g4nB1Hsfl90vZ8lgOm0Gk1AMJikZTLV8t7VTbRzTkdNOlXu880hUeSvcY00Lp6XsZXvzvmI706-99HFtWx4OFx495ZzqP8u0uG-Y8u-O9ucxTwc_AQAA__98SGYJ) beginning this May, ending a decades-old perk that set the carrier apart from its competitors. Business class customers and members of the carrier’s top-tier frequent flyer program will still get two bags checked for no additional charge, while Southwest credit card holders and members of the standard frequent flyer program will [get one free checked bag](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLGy2yAURL8GdXjgCoxdUKShe2lTapC4iDvB4gWQZf19RunT756dPb--pi9Pmbb1p3-h7Z9YJhCguRi5hCl4yuekhmBnEZ5yQCuNksaYEfSQbBi10B7ugA-9yPAUIqoZ7-rhtRHRhIHsBROjBCm0gfGm4TGjiibO8xN99EwJDNRLvfWEHT--xXyWN9bbUl5Dtqn378bGHwwcA3ccx21vvpfgzyvAwLVe6snA9erfmBk4TzXThnzDozFw1z4DJ0YGTsqrUPaeDmydU-OB-pJoW3msiHxJuPzGwPO-rn5FnrBi40cqvHXKmf_ZfaZIeHEfAHcAoYQwDNxQbfg-KGdqd8OUWF-e8r8L_b9O3xb-BgAA__90Cnjh). Over the past year, the airline has made [several other changes](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLHO4yAQBp8Gd2vBgoNdUFzj7r_2SmuBxUYidmS4OHn7U9Jf_UmfZubPz_JDueR9_U13du2VjgUlDiA1KFwi5fJeTBedl3FSHTtljbLWahy6zY0-RK08B699kJimaJRGY_1IGPWkuuw-Z1IrVHKwqPsBR88m2eT9xJRIGMkxt-Ps28aNX1RTeR9PPvtw3LvittYeVehfAmeB83Vd_ZWIPqPAmc6WQ2GB885XFTiXI1ARONfjb9surg0onyXvXMHTWiGdzBA22leuQLXmdecIx4N3qEwt7ytEKoUqfFEEzjhasHhTSlkJ6JUCoziBNzcD1soQ9CiDT7I7XXxcuZRcb1YYud4pl69D-2_Up8N_AQAA___oYXlD) to boost profits, like ending its open-seating policy, partnering with travel companies like Expedia to reach more customers, and cutting about 1,700 corporate jobs. United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby [characterized the development](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLFuwyAQQL8Gb0RwmJAMDF28pWtH64CzjURMZC5x_PdVund_ek96P7fxhrnkdf7GO3l-T3UEBVYqIzWMCXM5xr5LPqh01R157XrtnDNgu8VbBKXOOpiEMUZKOqIyEdAGbay69F32H5kyGrSyDszJwiVQP7kphCvhhKJXlDLX7cQLMb2xTeWoL9pOsd674hfmRxPmS8AgYOCFHjWv3Obn8QEEDCvtTcDQ6pOXnRpLzFvJKzUZcJYTUZN5Tc_G2yE3wsi5rgKGbvPpsedScjs70av5jrn8NfnfCS8PvwEAAP__AW9huw) as “the slaying of the sacred cow,” clarifying that he believed the move would be “good for everyone” in the industry.
## Best New Restaurants in Texas
_Texas Monthly_ released its annual list of the state's top 10 best new restaurants earlier this month, featuring independent establishments that opened between December 2023 and November 2024. Topping the list is [Austin’s Craft Omakase](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLuO6yAQhp8Gd7ZgMIekoDiNu2y7pTWYIUbCOIJxLm-_Sqpttv316b99X-YLppzK9Qs3cvyM-wwSTC91r2AOmPJrHrvgvAxn1ZFTdlTWWg2mW52Sehnj2fugF7IQrDYQT2aJcEIPOnbJvc2kVqCksaAHAydPY7TR-zNhRDFKCon3OvBKTE9sMb_2O9Vh2bcuu5X51oT-L2ASMOHROJVhOTIflTa8vSkBU6FHEzBVaoxHxcKt91jf0meLp8Z9oUf_G_iE9dteeM0vAVNXXbg9Us6p_bNilNcNU_604D9vuTv4CQAA__8P6meg), a sushi restaurant that was one of two in Texas to earn a star in the state’s inaugural Michelin Guide. Another Austin establishment, Mexican restaurant Mexta, was ranked No. 7 on the list. Dallas-Fort Worth is [home to three restaurants](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kDGv4yAQhH8N7jaCxYRzQZHG3bvudGWEzfKMhCGCTfzy709Of5pmNCN9Gs3fr_uXTzmV799-J8c_sd5RogGpQeE9-JTf93EIbpFhUgM5ZUdlrdVohs1pvZ4ig6iua5iMiWrC8WrXhSYlzZDcCZNaoZLGor4Y_LXQGG1clol89GKUFBLXduGNmH58j_ldX9Qua92H7DbmRxf6JnAWOB_Hcdl7OTuBMxV4doEzN_-i_DHpkQL5T3iyYK-Ft_yGDjl1hhphoc5Q6IBGnf2z-cIdOnumIwWCVNb8DAQaUoHgc_YdYm0MR228CZx9g9tN3SLxn6G58DhSzqlfrRjl9-5T_uzm_x75cvgvAAD__427eLg) on the list, including No. 2 Radici Wood Fired Grill in Farmers Branch, an Italian restaurant run by celebrity chef Tiffany Derry. Offering dinner for $200 a person, Japanese restaurant Mābo in Dallas was ranked No. 3, and The Chumley House in Fort Worth—where visitors can “fulfill the fantasy of traipsing through the home of a mid-century British aristocrat”—earned the No. 9 spot. [Three Houston area restaurants](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kD9vgzAUxD-N2R7yH6jD4IEOLFW6dkTP8XOwakxkOyH59lXYu53upLvT7-c8nzHEkK7fuJKpT7_NksseuAIhZ4chvuauccZyN4iGjNCd0For2TeL0b67aD8oPgji-qTV0HFhFb_YvrcnwZtg3mVcCSl4r6Vqe3my1HntrR0IPbKOkwt1y21dqNITi4-v7UG5vWxrE81S660wNTI5MTnt-96uJb0zJidKcC9MTjXjg-Ihwi04wrf5GzJCKEsNCJgc0IqQcCUHIcExBOuW6hJfBSyVCol2yFQq3jOmWmDzcICIoVQmJ8wwjmLEL_3ZZONue4gxlA_NOn5dMcTjb_0X4MPIvwAAAP__xslz2g) earned the No. 4, No. 5, and No. 6 spots: sushi bar Kira, Native American tasting menu restaurant Ishtia in Kemah, and Mexican counter-service diner Ema. name: GOP Battleground Fund
subject: This is not an April Fool’s Day joke
body:
Control of Congress is at stake

| | | | [](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/a7Kx/?__vbtrk=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
---
Friend, President Trump's trifecta is at risk.
Two critical House seats, **FL-01** and **FL-06** , are facing special elections right now and the Radical Left is throwing everything they’ve got into these races to defeat us and take the House.
This is about much more than just two House seats. This is the first electoral test for the GOP since Trump’s historic victory last November.
This is about maintaining the House GOP Majority as a whole which has been the vanguard for President Trump and his administration.
This is where we must draw the line in the sand. Our GOP House majority provides President Trump with the support he needs to fulfill his agenda and save our country.
Losing these races means that we will hand over the House to the DNC’s minions on a silver platter and any further attempt to fulfill **Agenda 47 will be dead on arrival****.**
The consequences of failing to hold the line are hard to overstate.

The first thing the Democrats will do if they take the House is move to impeach President Trump. If that happens we would be back to 2019 when we were fighting an uphill battle at every turn to overcome Leftist obstruction.
_**Securing our borders**_ , _**unleashing energy dominance**_ , _**reducing inflation**_ , and **_crushing Deep State corruption_** are all on the line.
We have fought too hard to deliver an America First agenda to just let our hard won victory slip away now.

_**[The House GOP Battleground Fund was created to ensure our team of experienced GOP operatives have the resources they need to stay in the fight and defend the House seats that will determine the balance of power in our country](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/a7Kx/?__vbtrk=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct).**_
[DEFEND THE HOUSE](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/a7Kx/?__vbtrk=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
We have won fights like these before but time is quickly running out to give our team in the field the support they need to make a difference. Both special elections will take place on **April 1st** and that date is rapidly approaching.
Right now, DNC operatives are arriving in the Sunshine State from all over the country...
And according to their leaked donor calls they are securing enough special interest cash to flip both seats **BLUE**.
Friend, if we do not take immediate action then we run the risk of being outspent in the final stretch of these races.
**__[We are calling in the cavalry and we need America First patriots from across the nation to help us secure FL-01 and FL-06](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/a7Kx/?__vbtrk=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)_._**
[SECURE VICTORY IN FLORIDA](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/a7Kx/?__vbtrk=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
Securing these seats means protecting the Trump trifecta.
Last year voters gave President Trump and the GOP control of the _**White House**_ , control of the _**Senate**_ , AND control of the _**House**_.
But if Democrats take back the House they will pass legislation to change our election laws, like allowing illegal immigrants to vote, that will rig future elections in their favor and make it harder for Republicans to secure a trifecta again.
**Democrats are already attempting to pass laws in New York City that would allow non-citizens to vote!**
If they succeed it may take a generation before we see the type of resounding mandate that the American People gave to Save America and usher in a new age of American greatness.
**Our actions now will determine if our children and future generations will inherit chaos or a free and prosperous nation.**
We are the firewall _**against open borders**_ , _**against socialist policies**_ that lead to sky high inflation, _**against radical gender ideology**_ that allows men in girls' private spaces, and _**against the Swamp**_ abusing power.
_**_[To maintain that firewall we need to make a stand and ensure that we send conservative warriors to Congress to represent FL-01 and FL-06. So please consider contributing whatever you can today to fuel our defense of the House](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/a7Kx/?__vbtrk=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)_.**_
[FUEL THE HOUSE GOP BATTLEGROUND FUND](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/a7Kx/?__vbtrk=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjc5MzM2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
Thank you for you time and your continued support of our team and the America First movement. It is because of you that we are able to continue fighting to save America.

name: History Facts
subject: A hidden fragment of the Bible was recently discovered

As detailed in a 2023 research paper, an Austrian medievalist examining texts in the Vatican Library discovered an ancient fragment of the Book of Matthew, which had been hidden for around 1,500 years under two other layers of text.

# [Historians recently discovered a hidden fragment of the Bible.](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=st0c9u&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
### [World History](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=st0c9u&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
[](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=st0c9u&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
| A s detailed in a 2023 [research paper](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=st0c9u&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com), an Austrian medievalist examining texts in the Vatican Library discovered an ancient fragment of the Book of Matthew, which had been hidden for around 1,500 years under two other layers of text. The biblical text is an interpretation of parts of Matthew 11 and 12 that had never been seen before. It’s from one of the earliest translations of the Bible, written in Old Syriac. The Old Syriac translation dates back to the [third century CE](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=st0c9u&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) — even before the New Testament canon was officially established — but was lost for centuries, and only four examples have been unearthed in modern times, including the 2023 discovery.
---
Some of the earliest versions of the Gospels — the four canonical New Testament books that tell the story of Jesus Christ — originated in Syria, which was home to major early Christian hubs such as Damascus and Antioch; these early versions were written in or translated to Old Syriac. The text unearthed in 2023 dates back to the sixth century, so it’s possible it was in widespread use before its disappearance.
When the earliest forms of the Bible were taking shape in the first few centuries CE, scholars wrote on parchment made from animal skin. (Paper didn’t reach the Middle East until the eighth century CE.) Since it wasn’t easy to come by, pieces of parchment were often erased and used for other works. Today, historians can use ultraviolet photography to reexamine materials that have already been in academic or religious libraries for a long time and see what was originally written beneath. In the case of the 2023 discovery, it’s believed the parchment containing the Old Syriac Gospel was [covered](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=st0c9u&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) by a Greek translation of the _Sayings of the Desert Fathers_ (a collection of stories about early Christian hermits in Egypt), which was covered again by a Georgian manuscript.
[](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=st0c9u&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) | [](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=st0c9u&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)

## Archaeologists discovered a 4,250-year-old library in Syria.
More than 4,000 years ago, the city of Ebla in northwestern Syria was a major hub of manufacturing, education, and agriculture. In 1974, archaeologists were excavating the former site of its royal palace when they discovered 42 tablets filled with cuneiform script. The palace, including the wooden shelves where the tablets were stored, had burned down around 2250 BCE, but the fire baked and [preserved](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=st0c9u&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) the clay tablets. Archaeologists kept digging and eventually found more than 17,000 cuneiform tablets, containing everything from commercial ledgers to literary works.

Dear Friend of Liberty,

[I'm writing to ask you to participate in Hillsdale College's **DEFEAT DEI SURVEY**](https://links.defend-the-constitution.org/s/c/V8ZpRY0O0cYiNd0XLLa99L8p2zeyei2bSSCsD-D8P9xwpqwSikumb60L4bUVQLHrDdn3_Iz7jpWuLOdw74ScmPIHgCdlbHCR3Lj3K2gHJfbQPfWrrXgOGHN_VdLeEAQ3NehQILaugy8mcs06t_91YhKrMy-w4e2hARSiQg2t7XuXCiTIoKrakKjPlHrTfJGy1_GkJsCYdsIZZCU6D_Ngemcl73K3Ak7ZHlQhxgth_YfEu3Ua5h2d8_H8dtlP9kcKG4D7iQOSkPLuGXusrySmR4cwziFEVjRTvT02o8fW_kX-LkeJzxzB-J2kA8jrGAlfg3d1ipBXgn_ctvJW0IcRU8uDwNxd6xdYIrm-fyLFq0EuZ01XrAG_zo1iilBSCmWdHOwjma9vRZeyCAEDEKUdxd4Y6q_KdMDumt8DICQUKFqN29nx3KQ2t5_Z_5pvR24/zPmI-CRs1JValx-_2uPJV3WYoAaxufSq/6).

DEI policies have infected almost every aspect of American life, from K-12 schools to college admissions and job applications. They have even spread into the hard sciences and the military.

These policies endanger lives and, ultimately, Western Civilization itself.

SB25-003 faces Constitutional hurdles under the Bruen standard
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi folks,
Don't forget to to listen to our new Mountain Minute Podcast, every morning! Click [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Colorado Legislative Session Updates...** SB25-003 could face legal challenges under the [Bruen standard](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with gun advocates calling it unconstitutional. HB 1208’s [proposed price controls](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) face criticism for potentially harming businesses. A bill imposing [$20,000 fines on gas stations](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for missing climate warning stickers raises concerns over government overreach. The universal preschool expansion [plan failed](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) due to logistical and funding issues.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Ukraine agreed to a [30-day cease-fire](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as the U.S. resumes military aid, while Russia’s participation remains unclear. DHS is replacing CBP One with CBP Home to modernize immigration processing and [encourage self-deportations](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
This is the Mountain Minute for Wednesday, March 12, 2025.
– Heidi Ganahl
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Anderson: SB25-003 faces Constitutional hurdles under the Bruen standard](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY PHILLIP ANDERSON, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Many conservatives and Second Amendment advocates have raised concerns about the constitutionality of SB25-003, a bill that seeks to make it significantly more difficult for Coloradans to exercise their Second Amendment rights. These advocates argue that if the bill becomes law, it will not withstand a constitutional challenge under the Bruen standard established by the Supreme Court of the United States.
If you do not closely follow Supreme Court cases or have never heard of the Bruen standard, you may be unsure what to make of these claims. The Bruen standard of review in Second Amendment cases originates from New York State Rifle & Pistol Association, Inc. v. Bruen. In this case, two New York residents challenged a state law that allowed officials to deny handgun carry licenses for self-defense unless an applicant could demonstrate a “special need.” The plaintiffs were denied licenses because they failed to cite such a need.

**[Colorado fuel retailers face up to $20,000 fine for failing to post warning stickers about global warming under proposed bill](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* House Bill 25-1277 would impose fines of up to $20,000 on Colorado fuel retailers who fail to post global warming warning stickers on gas pumps, store displays, and other petroleum-based products.
* Critics argue the bill is designed to shame consumers for using gasoline and diesel, which remain essential for many families and businesses. Lower-income households, unable to afford electric vehicles, would be unfairly targeted.
* The bill could extend to products like propane, butane, and fuel additives, raising concerns over enforcement, compliance costs, and whether minor violations—such as a missing or damaged sticker—would result in fines.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Universal preschool bill dies as some Colorado programs still complain of bumps](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado’s universal preschool program remains popular with families but continues to face logistical and financial struggles, prompting some providers to call for changes in state regulations and funding.
* A bill aimed at addressing these concerns was killed due to the state’s $1 billion budget shortfall, with lawmakers hesitant to allocate additional funds while an ongoing evaluation of the program is still underway.
* Preschool directors are pushing for earlier state payments and greater flexibility on class size limits, as new state-mandated caps will further tighten preschool operations in the coming years.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[House Bill 1208: Price controls for a minimum wage mistake](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COMPLETE COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* HB 1208 seeks to offset the impact of local minimum wage hikes by implementing a mandatory tip credit, allowing employers to count tips toward meeting wage requirements.
* Denver alone has seen 473 restaurant closures in the past three years, with business owners blaming high labor costs, regulatory burdens, and economic downturns.
* While some view HB 1208 as a band-aid fix, critics argue the real issue lies in local governments' ability to impose minimum wage laws above the state level. They advocate for repealing the 2019 law that allows municipalities to set their own wage floors, claiming it leads to economic disparity and job losses.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

name: Ben Samuels
subject: Three wacky but sensible policy ideas
body:
There's too much partisanship and too little creativity in lawmaking. Here are some ideas to fix that.

| |
---|---|---
| | | Forwarded this email? [Subscribe here](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.hLOYNbz9rZ6ggtEby95dm-NyTfzJPdTGWEGS-VHEUdk?) for more
---
# [Three wacky but sensible policy ideas](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=157405037&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTU3NDA1MDM3LCJpYXQiOjE3NDE3ODAzNjIsImV4cCI6MTc0NDM3MjM2MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.-qE-mC7UdbB9PgTMMYGUX_v7mnprJ2MEjRSb0xxghiY)
### There's too much partisanship and too little creativity in lawmaking. Here are some ideas to fix that.
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
| Mar 12
---
| [](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvYmVuc2FtdWVscy9wL3RocmVlLXdhY2t5LWJ1dC1zZW5zaWJsZS1wb2xpY3ktaWRlYXM_.jR5bShA10lUlsNlvDzboy9JWmniRTlMSCI6_fL2l9Ik?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/three-wacky-but-sensible-policy-ideas?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

For decades, long predating the challenges of this particular moment, one of the biggest issues in politics has been an inability to dream big. It's wild that a government-led effort put men on the moon in the '60s; such a thing feels completely impossible today.
But I would even take that one step further: there is a remarkable lack of creativity in policymaking. Obviously issues like gun safety, immigration, and tax policy matter a ton, but there are other things that we can do to improve society too.
Here are three out-there but sensible policies that would make things better, in big ways and small. I hope this spurs you, and your representatives, to think more creatively than anyone in Washington, D.C. (or in Jefferson City) seems to be thinking.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/30d2a9ec-fb0a-4229-8737-205dc743cd68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### 1\. The dollar should be denominated to one decimal place ($1.0), not two ($1.00)
You won't hear me say "the Trump administration is right" very often, but they're wise to [get rid of the penny](https://substack.com/redirect/49bc8ddf-b1d4-4674-9a08-2f56c73971cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).1 My only issue is that they're not taking it far enough.
We shouldn't even have theoretical pennies in transactions anymore, and the U.S. Dollar should only be denominated to the tenths place ($1.0), not to the hundredths place ($1.00).
A little bit of history: the U.S. dollar, technically, was denominated at one point to the thousandths place ($1.000), and the [half-penny](https://substack.com/redirect/eaee4ec6-173c-4e99-9325-4a32dded0f5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was a coin that existed in the earliest days of the country. But the half-penny died with the [Coinage Act of 1857](https://substack.com/redirect/e831e1fe-251c-41c5-aa65-8e3c4c219354?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), because it was determined that the half-penny--which would be [worth roughly 18¢ today](https://substack.com/redirect/c54e323c-d12d-4f85-807f-f1a210dddd92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--[had too little value](https://substack.com/redirect/5500df66-a8e9-4f70-bae4-ba764bb72e0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).2
It's high time to simplify things even further with the U.S. dollar--we're creating complexity and over-precision that's neither wanted3 nor needed. Any transaction between $1.00 and $1.04 would round down to $1.0; any transaction between $1.05 and $1.09 would round up to $1.1.4
What are the benefits?
1. Increased simplicity of transactions for vendors and customers.
2. The Mint would get to ditch [money-losing pennies and nickels](https://substack.com/redirect/0053909f-0f0e-49cc-bd6f-9aa1284e8283?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). They'd only have to make two coins--dimes and half-dollars--which would simplify the scope of their work.
3. Nothing that I'm aware of costs less than 10¢ these days. Sooner or later, we'll end up wanting to do this anyway.

Any concerns with this?
* _Would this increase costs to consumers?_ No, I don't think so. First of all, because it's well understood that [pricing ending with a nine encourages people to buy more](https://substack.com/redirect/28992d49-c553-48fb-acd7-e74b2089c18c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), I would argue that it'd actually end up _saving_ a small amount of money, because retailers would start pricing at simply $0.9 rather than $0.99 to capture the same benefit. But even without that, the average American consumer [transacts roughly 865 times per year](https://substack.com/redirect/a3530d57-9f11-4832-8fca-4e0c83b48be5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); over that many transactions, the rounding would generally net out.5
* _Would this create technical or logistical hurdles for businesses?_ We don't need to phase this in tomorrow; we can phase this in over a decade.6 It's worth noting that the UK and Australia underwent a significantly more complicated process called [decimalization](https://substack.com/redirect/423d85ce-ba96-4b9a-9bb9-530c70248531?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) back in the '60s and '70s, without the help of computers and in a much shorter period of time, and they did just fine.7

Plus, if we move to the one-decimal-point system, maybe we'll get a [delightfully wonderful video](https://substack.com/redirect/2ecf2b72-07e5-4f40-b254-1c724e998526?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) like this one from Australia in the mid-'60s.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/2ecf2b72-07e5-4f40-b254-1c724e998526?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### 2\. [Price controls](https://substack.com/redirect/1cc67a67-053c-478f-9059-d7183f862f86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are almost always bad. But there should be price caps on bottled water at stadiums built with any public funding
As I've [written about before](https://substack.com/redirect/ee7cb2dc-71dd-45cb-bfdc-4f697967a5fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), even though [public funding of stadiums is a bad use](https://substack.com/redirect/dd98d2e5-4a02-4331-99a7-7c2cc7ecdd54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of taxpayer money, it's quite common. Let's take the St. Louis Cardinals as an example.
The Cardinals got public funding [when they first built the new Busch Stadium](https://substack.com/redirect/c95924de-84dd-45a4-a9cb-b2fdd88c3d65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2006.8 Now, with the stadium not yet 20 years old, [they're asking for more cash from taxpayers](https://substack.com/redirect/119b733d-7a51-4b88-a8ac-32ddde9c92a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
It's certainly their right to try. But what strikes me as particularly obscene is to then use taxpayer-funded facilities to gouge people at games by [charging them $6 for a water](https://substack.com/redirect/cb26b0a9-e91a-4f12-821b-2bd49c914a58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).9
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cb26b0a9-e91a-4f12-821b-2bd49c914a58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Credit: [KSDK](https://substack.com/redirect/c9799289-bf29-49bd-86d7-0e9e4041332b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Look, charge whatever you want for beer.10 But I think any stadium that takes even a dime11 from taxpayers should be limited to charging $2 for bottled water.
* At wholesale prices, a 20 oz. bottle of Dasani costs less than $2. Teams would still be making money; we're not creating any hardship here.
* The issue with price caps is that they artificially increase demand (which can lead to shortages in supply). On the supply side, they're not going to run out of water--that's not really applicable here. And when it comes to increased demand, I say: good! We all should probably be drinking more water, especially if it's [90 degrees during a July day game](https://substack.com/redirect/3d4c1323-c425-4769-8115-93ca39209a08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at Busch.

This is an easy concession to the taxpayers, who are paying for someone else's glitzy new stadium. The very modest public health benefits12 are good too.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=157405037&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTU3NDA1MDM3LCJpYXQiOjE3NDE3ODAzNjIsImV4cCI6MTc0NDM3MjM2MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.-qE-mC7UdbB9PgTMMYGUX_v7mnprJ2MEjRSb0xxghiY)
### 3\. Teaching students about smallpox should be mandatory under state law
Vaccines and other medical advances that have [drastically reduced mortality in children](https://substack.com/redirect/63fe077c-7777-4247-88b3-786e7776e5ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are the greatest public health accomplishments in the history of the world. Of course, the two go hand-in-hand; infants who are unvaccinated are [nearly twice as likely to die as children who are vaccinated](https://substack.com/redirect/21b288f3-8c19-4876-bc0f-22fd255aa07a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/21b288f3-8c19-4876-bc0f-22fd255aa07a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Credit: [Our World in Data](https://substack.com/redirect/21b288f3-8c19-4876-bc0f-22fd255aa07a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Robert Kennedy, Jr. is an absolute quack, and although he's responsible for some of the decline in the public's faith in vaccines, his appointment to the Cabinet is also [responsive to a larger--and deeply alarming--trend among the American public](https://substack.com/redirect/f480040c-1b84-470a-b08a-0c3be28996b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).13
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f480040c-1b84-470a-b08a-0c3be28996b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Credit: [Gallup](https://substack.com/redirect/f480040c-1b84-470a-b08a-0c3be28996b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
All of the [controversy around the COVID-19 vaccine](https://substack.com/redirect/6644f48d-e2ab-44d4-bc35-243693a783b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) didn't help here. But some of this is a function of the fact that the people old enough to remember polio, smallpox, and other diseases are elderly or have already died. [We're a victim of our own success](https://substack.com/redirect/83f65410-f87b-4609-83c6-8c3e43ea328a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
It's important to help people understand how extraordinary the eradication of smallpox really was. **[Smallpox killed 300 million people in the 20th century](https://substack.com/redirect/b930d73a-2598-4f8f-bb61-75a192d5f460?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) --many multiples more than every war in the 20th century combined**,14 and the equivalent of nearly the entire U.S. population. But we've forgotten about smallpox alarmingly fast; I don't remember learning much about it in school.
So what can we do about this?
* **We should push for states to mandate education on smallpox and its eradication**. This really shouldn't be controversial; I've never seen any claim, even from staunch anti-vaccine nuts, that the smallpox vaccine was a bad thing. [Photos of smallpox victims](https://substack.com/redirect/5ae713a9-30f2-47a7-a146-886376a0f326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) speak for themselves.
* **Local science centers and museums should devote more energy to the history of infectious diseases**. As far as I can tell, there are no museums dedicated to smallpox specifically.15 In a period where childhood diseases are no longer common, this feels as important now as it's ever been.

Remembering a phenomenon that killed 300 million people in the 20th century feels important on its own merits. Understanding the miracle of the smallpox vaccine is a worthy goal too--and something that's obviously lost on far too many Americans today.
From the smallpox vaccine, people can extrapolate however they'd like as they think about hesitancy towards today's vaccines.
### Dream bigger and more creatively
Just because people haven't discussed certain ideas doesn't mean that they don't matter or wouldn't help.
It's not like these ideas are going to fix the world--our political division isn't solved by $2 bottles of water. But thinking creatively is the first step to dreaming bigger, and we seem to have lost the ability to do both.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTU3NDA1MDM3LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzQxNzgwMzYyLCJleHAiOjE3NDQzNzIzNjIsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.5q-LgCcRVg6Jp5ZHMT7dFmHywmVmIVH1k4Oci22MI34?)
_**Feel free to share this post with someone who will find this interesting.** (If you're reading this email because someone sent it to you, [please consider subscribing](https://substack.com/redirect/30d2a9ec-fb0a-4229-8737-205dc743cd68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)_

1
This has been on my mind since 2008--shout-out to those of us who took AP English Language that year!
[Here's the first exam prompt](https://substack.com/redirect/1c835dbd-ae63-4a43-aef7-55dbdde226ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), if you somehow missed that year's AP test: "In 2001 United States Representative [Jim Kolbe](https://substack.com/redirect/e9fb80dd-3a50-487f-95ae-2506b6c9899c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) introduced legislation to Congress to eliminate the penny coin in most transactions... _Assignment_ : Read the following sources (including the introductory information) carefully. Then write an essay in which you develop a position on whether or not the penny coin should be eliminated."
2
The whole conversation around getting rid of the half-penny has shades of [this scene from ](https://substack.com/redirect/207a1c22-ad74-4670-9000-936f2fb7d52c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[A Million Ways to Die in the West](https://substack.com/redirect/207a1c22-ad74-4670-9000-936f2fb7d52c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_.
3
Americans throw away--literally, throw into the trash--[$68 million per year in coins](https://substack.com/redirect/2a97404d-5dc6-4c51-a759-4bb99441bd28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which tells us something about how much people value coins. And that says nothing about all the coins in the purgatory of car seats or couch cushions.
4
We already do this with sales taxes, which we could calculate to the thousandths place or beyond if we wanted to.
5
Three notes on this:
* The rounding would happen, for most items, _after_ state and local sales taxes, so it'd be pretty hard for retailers to game this and gain any meaningful benefit.
* However, if you assume that every single retailer rounded up on every single transaction, this would cost Americans (roughly) $44 more per year. But again: I reject that that'd happen, in large part because retailers would have a strong incentive to drop prices from $9.99 to $9.9 rather than to $10.0, for the psychology reasons I noted above.
* If we assume that after including sales taxes, the odds of rounding up or down are 50/50, then the chances that any given American would randomly get rounded up on every single transaction would be infinitesimally small--we're talking 10^(-255) small. Across this many transactions, the odds of any one American being unlucky (or lucky) to the tune of even $15 over the entire year would be exceedingly unlikely.

6
Almost everything is done digitally today, and that would give everyone plenty of time for anyone's point-of-sale software to conform to new rules in a way that wouldn't cost anyone anything.
7
The [old system with the British pound](https://substack.com/redirect/8e2f0566-272a-4fcc-ba47-c1d66ef0466a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was almost comically arcane: there were four farthings in a pence, 12 pence in a shilling, and 20 shillings in a pound. (I don't envy 19th-century British accountants.) It's what inspired the [even more arcane monetary system in ](https://substack.com/redirect/8697610f-7b96-4d20-b501-a27eeec0cf32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[Harry Potter](https://substack.com/redirect/8697610f-7b96-4d20-b501-a27eeec0cf32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , if you were wondering.
8
This data comes directly from the Cardinals, so it should be taken with a grain of salt. Other sources suggest that [taxpayers spent much more than the team claims](https://substack.com/redirect/0551bb11-5d61-44e3-8b1f-27bd088b80b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
9
By the way: [you ](https://substack.com/redirect/5bbd2798-c163-4d73-9f25-b6cba9a98a40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[are](https://substack.com/redirect/5bbd2798-c163-4d73-9f25-b6cba9a98a40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ allowed to bring outside food and non-alcoholic beverages into games](https://substack.com/redirect/5bbd2798-c163-4d73-9f25-b6cba9a98a40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), at least at Busch Stadium. But a lot of people don't know this, and of course, it's not broadly advertised. Also, this menu is from 2023, so it's possible that prices went up last year; I'm not sure and couldn't find an obvious answer online.
10
Busch Stadium is [middle-of-the-pack when it comes to beer prices](https://substack.com/redirect/035e100c-3e22-42a9-8938-a91b91a5080f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) but has some of the most expensive hot dogs of any stadium in the country. Policy remedies notwithstanding, I'd prefer they do [what the Phoenix Suns are doing](https://substack.com/redirect/921947a1-6cd2-43c5-8ea6-da9771f2af52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and lower prices of their own volition.
11
See, who needs the penny!
12
Namely: a) [hydration is good](https://substack.com/redirect/2d2394bf-c930-4fa4-86ed-a25a97a3ce27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and lowering the price will mean more people buy water, and b) there'd probably be some very slight mix shift from people drinking beers who'd instead drink water, which would reduce (among other things) drunk driving rates. I'll concede that I don't have data to back this up--you'd have to model it out--but this would make sense against a standard framework of pricing and economics, even if the benefits are relatively minor.
13
There are _[extremely](https://substack.com/redirect/f480040c-1b84-470a-b08a-0c3be28996b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ stark differences by political affiliation](https://substack.com/redirect/f480040c-1b84-470a-b08a-0c3be28996b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which is even more alarming. It's a [huge part of what we're seeing play out in West Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/06de44ca-fe07-4bb9-90cb-008f34fbfa69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), where many counties [vote 85%+ for Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/a4e327ec-bea1-41c7-ae78-a06457495427?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
And if you ever find yourself wondering what the Founding Fathers would've thought about all of this, Benjamin Franklin--whose [four-year-old son](https://substack.com/redirect/4655596d-7192-4344-823d-4b3682978302?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) died of smallpox--became a [staunch advocate of smallpox inoculation for the rest of his life](https://substack.com/redirect/226bd468-9705-4a20-aa38-8ceebca0c08c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). (The vaccine, as we conceive of it today, [wasn't invented until 1796](https://substack.com/redirect/588fea8b-43dd-4c5b-aed2-ab9043fd978e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but there were earlier, if significantly less effective, methods of trying to prevent its spread and to reduce the fatality rates among the infected.)
14
This is true, by the way, even if you include civilian deaths (e.g., the Holocaust) and diseases whose spread was advanced by war (e.g., the [Spanish flu](https://substack.com/redirect/f69fad69-b150-4102-8f1d-6e188d79a680?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). It's truly difficult to fathom just how many people died of smallpox, and it's jarring to think how quickly we've forgotten about it.
15
In the UK, there's a [museum about Edward Jenner](https://substack.com/redirect/261bba8a-1783-4855-a8c1-14895ae08440?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who invented the first smallpox vaccine, but that's more about his life than the vaccine or the disease. In Atlanta, what could be best described as a [small corner of the CDC Museum](https://substack.com/redirect/d503c0e4-0244-4bf4-8afb-cdb3625556c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is dedicated to smallpox eradication. But that's really it.

But some of this is a function of the fact that the people old enough to remember polio, smallpox, and other diseases are elderly or have already died. . It's important to help people understand how extraordinary the eradication of smallpox really was. --many multiples more than every war in the 20th century combined,14 and the equivalent of nearly the entire U.S. population. We should push for states to mandate education on smallpox and its eradication. This really shouldn't be controversial; I've never seen any claim, even from staunch anti-vaccine nuts, that the smallpox vaccine was a bad thing. speak for themselves. Local science centers and museums should devote more energy to the history of infectious diseases. Understanding the miracle of the smallpox vaccine is a worthy goal too--and something that's obviously lost on far too many Americans today. From the smallpox vaccine, people can extrapolate however they'd like as they think about hesitancy towards today's vaccines. # Women and girls are worth fighting for.
---
| | | | | | | | | | [](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=826e55d34b&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
| [Watch Video ](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=a722119f84&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
| | | | | I’ve spent my career standing up for women and girls. Not because it was easy— but because it was necessary.When I first stepped into this work, I didn’t know just how much it would shape me.
How much it would challenge me.
How much it would _matter_.Years ago, I had the extraordinary privilege of working on [girls empowerment ](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=b09bd46903&e=edbde6c9b1)programs through Sesame Workshop —the global nonprofit behind Sesame Street. There, I poured my energy into supporting initiatives that gave young girls a voice—not just to sing or smile, but to be strong, to be curious, to lead, to dream big. Because I believed then—and still do—that when girls see themselves reflected, they start to believe in their power.Now I’m back in my home town of Spartanburg, South Carolina—a place I love deeply.
But let’s be honest: there’s work to do here. There are things happening in this state that deeply affect women—our choices, our bodies, our futures.And while I may not be working for women and girls around the globe anymore, I’m still fighting here at home with amazing organizations like the [Women’s Rights & Empowerment Network](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=d2c64efc5e&e=edbde6c9b1). Because there is still so much _worth fighting for_.This Women’s History Month, I’m reminded of the women who came before us—who marched, who taught, who healed, who built, who sacrificed.
And I’m reminded that history isn’t just something we read about.
It’s something we create—every single day.So, if you’re wondering whether your voice matters, whether your advocacy is too small, whether your presence can make a difference—let me tell you: it does.And we need you to stay in this fight.
